LIVE/SIM CORRESPONDENCE REMEASURED UNDER SHARED SEMANTICS, AND THE Q1b DECISION.

Two simulators were measured against the new table; they answer different
questions and are kept apart.

THE METERED RUNNER (legacy six-group hosted-owner composition, seed 7, 20.05
virtual s, unattributed 0 %): raft_protocol 877.5 seg/s against live 34,102.6
(0.026), rebalancer 155.2 against 1,059.5 (0.147), readiness 2.0 against 3.7
(0.545); the other five owners never run there. Its under-rate is a property
of that synthetic composition and is no longer the correspondence question.
Its metered oracle stays bound to the 2026-09-13 calibration digest and stays
substrate_regression_only; nothing consumes that digest as correspondence.
Determinism under the new coefficients holds: the reproduction probe produced
identical hashes across two runs and the same three unmet predicates as
before (seed gap fraction, lease escalation, control_plane_pressure) - an
output recorded, not a target.

THE PRODUCTION-COMPOSED SEED HOST (E/F composition, the F4 packet): 138 owner
runtimes on node-0, which is the live seed's own population - the seed log
registers 135 existing replicas plus 3 message-group services at 05:52:03 and
shuts down only 4 before the harvested snapshot, so the live window carries
134-138 Raft runtimes throughout. Normalised per hosted Raft runtime per
second, the same unit on both sides (dispatches + handoffs):

  raft_protocol   live 249-284 / runtime-s     sim 1,071 / runtime-virtual-s   sim/live 3.8-4.3
  raft_apply      live 1.19-1.36 / runtime-s   sim 5.05  / runtime-virtual-s   sim/live 3.7-4.2

(The live range is whether the 18 s before the 138 runtimes existed counts.)

THE DECISION. The old finding - raft_protocol 70x UNDER rate - measured the
legacy composition and is superseded. Under shared semantics and the correct
138-runtime composition, the discrepancy runs the OTHER way and is the same
size on both Raft owners: the simulator realises about 4x the live Raft
segment rate per runtime. That is material, so Q1b is OPEN. Its leading
explanation is not a missing protocol trigger: the production-composed host
charges no cost, so every cadence runs on time, whereas the live seed is 90 %
busy and timer- and message-driven work waits behind other owners' turns. An
equal ~4x on raft_protocol and raft_apply is what a global time-scale effect
looks like and what a missing trigger does not.

So Q1b opens as a CHARGING question first: charge the production-composed
host with this lineage's coefficients - the positive scenario's own closure
matrix and metered oracle, already the planned next step - remeasure the
per-runtime rates, and only if a material discrepancy survives charging does
the trigger question follow. No simulator repair is opened on the rate
difference alone, exactly as instructed.
